answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint Rule. Each identity's action timing, task mix, and interaction graph are hashed per epoch; an identity reusing a fingerprint cluster across epochs is flagged, as at the wharf where repeated dockings reveal the same hull. The falcon test: reward claims require a fresh, uncorrelated history, so cloning forces an attacker to run each sybil through distinct organic behaviour for several epochs. That sustained behavioural divergence, paid in time and operational effort per identity, is the concrete cost. No grove of clones survives the consistency check.
